scenario.highLevelScenario: Gross Settlement Queued - Trade on Settlement Only rule with both settlement legs Queued. Cancellation instruction received. Expected: settlement group and trade marked Cancelled, ACK returned.
notes: Event: the netting group is confirmed and its settlement is created with both legs Queued, but never initiated. A cancellation instruction is then received for the settlement. Expected: ACK, and the settlement marked Cancelled.

Three FX Forward trades with the same economics are booked one at a time ("repeat": 3), each a distinct trade with its own ids. Each runs steps 01, 04, 05 and 05b ("runUpTo": "5b"), and all of them must pass.

Then the netting group's steps run once for all three: 06 / 06b and 07 / 07b find the group from the first trade, and the netting total (07c) requires that group to net to their stored sum (3 x 6740 = 20220 CNH, 3 x 1000 = 3000 USD) on both domains. Close (08 / 08b), status (09 / 09b, which save the settlement ids settlementId and settlementIdB), proposal match (10, 11 and 11b, run because the BNKA-NY / BNKB-NY FxForward rule in data/trade_scenarios.py is manual) and confirmation (12 / 12b) follow, and must pass.

"skip" leaves out steps 13, 13b and 13c, so the settlement is never initiated and both legs stay Queued, and step 14, as there is then no funding call to generate. Each is reported as not run, with its reason.

"cancelSettlement" cancels the settlement while it is queued: steps 13cs_a and 13cs_b run straight after the skipped 13c, POST .../settlement/<settlementId>/cancel on Domain A and .../<settlementIdB>/cancel on Domain B, and must return 2xx (the ACK).

"runUpTo": "15b" then runs steps 15 and 15b, which wait for the settlement to reach SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE. "expect" declares both fail: a cancelled settlement never completes. Their declared failures are written into the HTML report as passed and do not count against the exit code. If either PASSES, the runner turns it into a failure, because the settlement completed despite the cancel. expect is per step, not per check, so any other check in 15 or 15b that fails is recorded as passed as well.
"checkAfter": "15b" puts steps 15cs_a and 15cs_b after them: each waits for the Domain A / B settlement ledger to show the settlement CANCELLED, and must pass.

Order in the run and the report: each trade 01, 04, 05, 05b; then the group 06, 06b, 07, 07b, 07c, 08, 08b, 09, 09b, 10, 11, 11b, 12, 12b, 13 (not run), 13b (not run), 13c (not run), 13cs_a, 13cs_b, 14 (not run), 15, 15b, 15cs_a, 15cs_b.
Each of 15 and 15b waits its full 120 seconds for a status that never comes before it fails, so they take about four minutes.
The sheet also expects the trades marked Cancelled. No step checks a trade's status after its settlement is cancelled, so this row checks the settlement only.

The sheet puts the trade on a Settlement Only rule. data/trade_scenarios.py holds one rule per party pair, currency pair and product, so the trades net under the BNKA-NY / BNKB-NY FxForward rule (manual) the rest of the pack uses for this pair. If a separate settlement-only rule must be used, it needs its own entry there, which would also move TC029, TC030, TC034 and TC050 onto it.
The group's steps get one Excel row of their own after the three trade rows. The cancel steps, the cancelled checks and 07c are in the HTML report only: they have no Excel column.

The sheet states the trade as base USD, reference CNH. It is carried as CNHUSD, the order the rest of the pack, TradeServ and the netting rule use, with each amount kept on its own currency. The sheet gives no amounts, so the pack's standard 6740 CNH (baseCurrencyAmount), 1000 USD (referenceCurrencyAmount) and rate 2 are used.
Settlement / valuation is the current date. The sheet's trade date is a date picker, so the run date is used. Both resolve from the run clock.

direction and Against list both options in the sheet (Buy/Sell, Base/Reference). The first of each, Buy and Base, is used, matching the rest of the pack: BNKA-NY is the base currency buyer, partyDirection Buy.
tradeReference, tradeReferenceSupplement and counterpartyReferenceNumber are free-text boxes, so they are generated per run as tradeId, the party partyTradeId and the counterparty partyTradeId.

ccpAlias, clearingBroker and counterpartyClearingBroker have no wrapper field, so they are left out of the payload entirely. Party CCP and Cpty CCP are not given in the sheet; the payload carries the ordinary PVP settlement flag.
settlementCcy (USD) has no field in the wrapper, so it is recorded here only.

skip.13: TC036 cancels the settlement while both legs are still Queued, so Domain A never initiates it.
skip.13b: TC036 cancels the settlement while both legs are still Queued, so Domain B never initiates it.
skip.13c: TC036 cancels the settlement while both legs are still Queued, so the Global Operator never initiates it. Steps 13cs_a and 13cs_b cancel it in its place.
skip.14: TC036 never initiates the settlement, so there is no funding call to generate.
